newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador suspends Millon Air in wake of crash.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador suspends Millon Air in wake of crash.

text.p: Ecuador's civil aviation authority on Friday suspended the operating permit of U.S. cargo carrier Millon Air three days after one of its jets crashed into a poor city neighborhood, killing 25 people.
"The suspension of the company from operating was decided for security reasons and as a preventative measure," the head of the authority's flight standards department, Fidel Guitarra, told Reuters.

The Boeing 707 cargo plane crashed in flames on Tuesday night, showering burning wreckage and jet fuel in the heart of the port city of Manta. Apart from those killed, 60 people were injured, many with severe burns.
Guitarra said the duration of Millon's suspension will depend on the results of a probe into the cause of the accident.
Ecuadoran officials, along with representatives of Boeing and engine-maker Pratt & Whitney are trying to determine the cause of the crash. The black box flight recorder has been found.
The Miami-bound jet with a cargo of frozen fish and flowers burst into flames 10 minutes after takeoff from Manta airport.

Millon Air is a Miami-based carrier owned by Colombians that operates charter freight flights to Latin America. In April 1995, a Millon DC-8 overran a runway in Guatemala City and crashed into a shantytown, killing six people on the ground.
A Millon representative in Ecuador confirmed the suspension and said that the company was discussing the matter with aviation authorities.
A cordon of soldiers and police were still sealing off the crash site on Friday to avoid possible looting. The last of the dead were buried on Thursday.
